## In this lesson
You'll install Hermes Agent, connect a model, teach it about you, give it a skill and a scheduled job that messages you on Slack, run it free on a local model, and create a second bot.

## Good to know
- Time: 45 to 60 minutes for everything. 10 minutes to say hello.
- Cost: Hermes is free and open source. You pay for the model: your existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription, or nothing with a local model.
- Level: Beginner to Intermediate
- It doesn't replace Claude Code. Claude Code is the specialist you open inside a project. Hermes runs everything around it, even after you close the laptop.

## What you need
- A computer to run it on (more below)
- One model, pick one:
  - Your Claude subscription, ChatGPT/Codex subscription, or Nous Portal
  - Ollama for free local models: https://ollama.com
- Slack, optional, for messages on your phone: https://slack.com

**1. Pick where it lives (1:35)**
Four options:
- A dedicated machine like a Mac mini or Mac Studio (can also run local models)
- A VPS. Hostinger has a Hermes setup ready to go.
- A spare laptop or old computer
- The computer you already use (it can still run 24/7)

**2. Install it (2:30)**
Website: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com
- Terminal version (Mac, Linux, Windows WSL):

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

- Desktop app (what I use for the rest of the video): on the same site, click "Download for macOS".

**3. Connect a model and say hello (4:00)**
Settings (top right) > Providers. Pick Anthropic (Claude), ChatGPT/Codex, or Nous Portal.
For Claude: copy the command it shows, paste it into a terminal, approve in the browser, then click "I've signed in". It says Connected.
Start a new session and type hello. You can switch models under the chat box.

**4. Tell it about yourself (5:05)**
Paste this into Claude (or whatever AI you already use) so it writes your intro for you:

> Write a short paragraph about me that I can hand to a new AI assistant. Plain text.

Then paste the answer into Hermes with: "Here's a bit about myself, save this." You'll see "saved to memory".

**5. See where memory lives (6:40)**
Memory is plain files you can open and edit. They're capped on purpose so they stay short and useful.

**6. Connect Slack so it can message your phone (10:20)**
Capabilities > Messaging > Slack, and follow the setup steps there.

**7. Turn a task into a skill (11:40)**
Do a task with it once. Then ask it to save that as a skill. Next time you ask for the same thing, it uses the skill. A skill is just a markdown file.

**8. Schedule a job (14:40)**
Scheduled jobs (top left) > New cron.
- Name it, write what it should do (mine checks my GitHub for failed runs and open PRs)
- Pick when (daily, or something like "weekdays at 9am")
- Deliver to Slack
- Click "Trigger now" to test it

**9. Run it free on your computer with Ollama (25:25)**
Install Ollama, then in a terminal:

```
ollama launch hermes
```

It offers to download the model if you don't have it.
To use the local model in the desktop app: Settings > Providers > Custom endpoints > add one:
- Name: Ollama
- Provider ID: ollama-launch
- URL: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
- API key: any word (I typed test). It's ignored.
It should say the endpoint is reachable and list your models.

**10. Make a second bot (22:40)**
Profiles let you create separate bots, each with its own memory, skills and jobs. Mine are a code reviewer and a researcher.

**11. Have bots hand work to each other (28:20)**
Open a bot's "Bot Chat" session and tell it to message another bot, like "tell @coder to review the latest commit". The other bot does the work and reports back.

## Files and links
- Hermes Agent: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com
- Docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/
- GitHub: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent
- Ollama: https://ollama.com

## If it breaks
- A bot won't hand off to another bot: you have to be in the session called "Bot Chat". Other sessions, including Slack, can't do hand-offs.
- Typing @botname in Slack does nothing: each bot needs its own Slack app for that. Slack is where bots message you; the desktop app is where you talk to them.
- The local model errors out right after you pick it: it's usually the context length. Try the same model with a larger context option, or a smaller model.
- Claude keeps asking you to log in again: re-run the provider sign-in command from Settings > Providers.

## In this lesson
You'll install DeepSeek Harness, connect a model (cheap cloud or 100% free on your own computer), and have it hand long jobs to Claude Code on the subscription you already pay for.

## Good to know
- Time: 20 to 30 minutes
- Cost: free with a local model. About $10 of OpenRouter credit if you use the cloud route.
- Level: Intermediate (you'll use a terminal)
- It's a developer preview. Things change and break. It doesn't replace Claude Code today.

## What you need
- Node.js (free): https://nodejs.org
- One model, pick one:
  - OpenRouter account with about $10 of credit (paid, cheap): https://openrouter.ai
  - Ollama for free local models: https://ollama.com
- Claude Code with a Claude Pro or Max plan, only for the sub-agent part: https://claude.com/claude-code

**1. Install and open it (1:39)**
Open a terminal and run:

```
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

It opens in your browser at http://127.0.0.1:3080 . When it asks for a DeepSeek API key, click "Configure later". You don't need one.
Skip the desktop version. It's made by a third party, not DeepSeek.

**2. Connect a model with OpenRouter (3:12)**
- Get an API key at openrouter.ai and add about $10 of credit.
- In Harness: Settings > Models > Add provider > openrouter > paste the key (or sign in) > Apply.
- Pick a model in the chat box. I used deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash. It's cheap and handles tools.
OpenRouter's free models exist, but they're rate limited and an agent will hit the limit fast.

**3. Or run it 100% free on your computer with Ollama (4:31)**
- Install Ollama and download a model (I used Gemma 4).
- Start Ollama with a bigger context window so the agent doesn't run out of room:

```
OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000 ollama serve
```

- In Harness: Settings > Models > Add custom provider (the second button, not "Add provider"). Fill in:
  - Display name: Ollama
  - API base URL: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
  - API protocol: openai-completions
  - API key: leave it blank (or type ollama)
- Click "Fetch available models", pick yours, and save. A green dot means it's connected.

**4. Watch everything the agent does with Trajectory (5:58)**
Start a new workspace and ask it to build something small, like "create a simple Flask to-do app". Open the Trajectory tab to see every step: your prompt, the context, the skill it picked, each tool call and the result.

**5. Let it build its own tools with Creator mode (8:25)**
Settings > General > Agent preset > Creator mode. Then ask for something like "add a plugin for a calculator overlay in the bottom right". Everything in Harness is a plugin (165 of them, even the sidebar), so you can switch pieces on and off.

**6. Hand long jobs to Claude Code (11:25)**
This uses your Claude subscription, not an API key. Claude Code has to be installed and logged in on the same computer.
Install the plugin, then restart Harness:

```
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code
dsh --profile web
```

Then turn the delegation tool on. The easiest way is to ask Harness: "enable the Claude Code sub-agent plugin". If you'd rather edit it yourself, it lives in ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml:

```
- id: tool-subagent
  disabled: false
  config:
    provider: claude-code
    toolName: subagent_claude_code
    backgroundMode: one-shot
    permissionMode: acceptEdits
```

Restart again, then try: "delegate a task to the Claude Code sub-agent to write a simple Fibonacci function". The hand-off shows up in Trajectory.

## Files and links
- DeepSeek Harness on GitHub: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
- Quick start: https://deepseek.com/harness/en/
- OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai
- Ollama: https://ollama.com
- Composio's plugin list: https://composio.dev/content/best-deepseek-harness-plugins

## If it breaks
- Ollama model won't connect: you used "Add provider" instead of "Add custom provider". Ollama needs the custom one.
- Local model stalls mid-task: Ollama was started without the bigger context. Quit the Ollama app and run the OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH command above.
- Claude Code task comes back having done nothing: permissionMode is still the default, which blocks edits. Set it to acceptEdits.
- New plugin doesn't show up: restart Harness. Every plugin change needs a restart.
- It restarted its own server and broke (happened to me on camera): run npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web again.
- One plugin from the Composio list added a pile of skins and wrecked the UI for me. If a plugin makes a mess, disable it and restart.

## In this lesson
You'll build a research agent that pulls the top content on any topic from YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and X, reads what's working, and hands you a brief with ideas. Then you'll put it on a schedule so it runs without you.

## Good to know
- Time: 30 to 45 minutes
- Cost: Claude Pro or Max plan. Apify gives you $5 of free credit to start, then it's paid.
- Level: Beginner. No code. You describe the agent and Claude builds it.

## What you need
- Claude Pro or Max plan, with Claude Code installed: https://claude.com/claude-code
- Apify account (the tool that collects the social media data): https://apify.com
- Matt Pocock's skills, for the "grilling" skill in step 4: https://github.com/mattpocock/skills

**1. Pick where to build it (0:22)**
Claude on the web, the Claude desktop app, or Claude Code in the terminal. I use Claude Code. Make sure you're in auto mode.

**2. Describe the agent (0:59)**
Paste this into Claude Code (swap the topic and platforms for yours):

> Create a Claude Code skill called social-me. It takes a topic, researches it across multiple platforms using Apify, reads the top YouTube video transcripts, finds what's working and the content gaps, and gives me a brief with content ideas. Ground everything in real data. Never invent numbers.

It creates a folder in ~/.claude/skills/social-me with a SKILL.md file. On a Mac, press Command + Shift + Period in Finder to see the hidden .claude folder.

**3. Give it tools with the Apify MCP server (2:45)**
- Sign in at apify.com, then go to https://mcp.apify.com
- Choose Claude Code, turn on "Add Apify token", and copy the command it gives you into your terminal
- In Claude Code type /mcp, pick Apify, and click Authenticate
- Exit Claude Code and open it again so it loads the new skill. Then type /social-me to run it.

**4. Make it better with the grilling skill (8:00)**
Install Matt Pocock's skills (it's an official Claude Code plugin now). Then type:

```
/grilling
```

Tell it: "I want to harden social-me." It asks you rounds of questions about what's weak and fixes the skill as you answer. Mine found that Instagram was returning hours-old posts with no engagement, and switched to a list of accounts to watch.

**5. Put it on a schedule (12:11)**
Two options:
- /loop runs it on your computer. Easy, but your computer has to stay on, and you set it up again after a restart.
- /schedule makes a Claude routine in the cloud that runs even when your computer is off. I used this one:

```
/schedule social-me every two days at 7am
```

Check it at claude.ai > Routines. The time shows in UTC, so adjust it to your time zone.

## Files and links
- The finished skill: https://github.com/tylerprogramming/claude-skills/tree/main/social-me
- Apify: https://apify.com
- Apify MCP setup: https://mcp.apify.com
- Matt Pocock's skills: https://github.com/mattpocock/skills

## If it breaks
- /social-me doesn't show up: Claude Code only loads new skills when it starts. Exit and open it again.
- Apify shows "needs authentication": run /mcp, pick Apify, authenticate.
- The routine runs at the wrong hour: routines use UTC. Change the time at claude.ai > Routines.
- The first version gives weak results: that's normal. That's what step 4 is for.

## In this lesson
You'll connect your apps (ClickUp, Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack) once through Arcade.dev and use them in Claude Code, the Claude desktop app, your own Python agents (LangChain and CrewAI), and agents that run on a schedule.
You'll also build your own MCP server without writing code, deploy it so it runs 24/7, and set up a morning briefing that runs every day at 7am. No passwords or tokens stored in a file.

## Good to know
- Time: 2 to 3 hours if you do every module. Steps 1 to 3 alone take about 20 minutes.
- Cost: Arcade is free to sign up. The Python agents need an OpenAI or Anthropic API key (paid per use). A Hostinger VPS is about $7 to $8 a month, and only if you want it running 24/7.
- Level: Beginner for steps 1, 2 and 8 (no code). Steps 3 to 7 use the terminal, but Claude writes the code and the course repo has it all.
- Honest caveat: Claude Routines don't run exactly at 7am. Mine finish a few minutes after.

## What you need
- Arcade account (sign in with Google), free: https://www.arcade.dev/
- Claude Code: https://claude.com/claude-code
- Claude desktop app (for steps 2 and 8)
- The free course code: https://github.com/tylerprogramming/arcade-course (runs on uv, a Python tool step 5 installs)
- An OpenAI key (https://platform.openai.com) or an Anthropic key (https://console.anthropic.com), for steps 5 to 7
- Accounts for the apps you connect. I used ClickUp, Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack and GitHub.
- Optional: a Hostinger VPS: https://www.hostinger.com

**1. Make your first MCP gateway and add it to Claude Code (0:56)**
A gateway is just a bundle of tools from the apps you pick. In the Arcade dashboard, go to MCP Gateways, click Create MCP Gateway, name it (mine was ClickUp Assistant), search for ClickUp and tick it, choose "members of this project", then click Create. Pick Claude Code and copy the command Arcade gives you. Paste it in your terminal. The course repo writes it like this:
```
claude mcp add arcade --transport http "https://api.arcade.dev/mcp/<your-slug>"
```
Open Claude Code, switch to auto mode (Shift + Tab), then type:
```
/mcp
```
Pick your gateway and press Enter to authenticate. A browser window opens on Arcade. Click allow. Then try it:
> For my ClickUp assistant, can you get me all my in progress tasks?
Writing works too. I asked it to add a comment to a task and it showed up in ClickUp.

**2. Use the same gateway in the Claude desktop app (7:27)**
In Arcade, open your gateway, click Connect, choose Claude desktop and copy the URL. In the Claude app go to Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector. Paste the URL, click Add, then Connect, and allow it on Arcade. You can set each tool to always allow or needs approval. Same tools, and you only connected once.

**3. Build your own MCP server without writing code (11:21)**
For a tool that's yours, like your own product. I asked Claude Code to do the install and setup for me. The two commands are:
```
uv tool install arcade-mcp
arcade new my_server
```
It comes with example tools (greet, whisper secret, star a repo). Run it on your computer from the my_server/src/my_server folder:
```
uv run server.py
```
Ask Claude for the command to add this local server to Claude Code, exit Claude Code, paste it, open Claude again and type /mcp to see my_server and its tools. Test it:
> Use the greet tool from my_server with the name Tyler
When it said there was no Arcade API key, I logged in from inside Claude Code (the ! runs a terminal command):
```
!arcade login
```

**4. Deploy your server so it runs 24/7 (18:03)**
Running it locally means your computer has to stay on. From the top folder of the project (the one with pyproject.toml), run:
```
arcade deploy -e src/my_server/server.py
```
When it says the deployment is successful, it shows up in the Arcade dashboard under Servers (not MCP Gateways). Make a new gateway with just the tool you want (I picked star a repo), add it to Claude Code like step 1, and authenticate in /mcp. Disable the old local my_server in /mcp so Claude uses the hosted one.

**5. Get the code and your keys ready (24:32)**
In the Arcade dashboard, make an API key (Dashboard > API Keys). Then install uv and set up the course code:
```
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
git clone https://github.com/tylerprogramming/arcade-course.git
cd arcade-course
uv sync
cp .env.example .env
```
Open .env and fill in ARCADE_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY (or set LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic and add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), and ARCADE_USER_ID (your email).

**6. Run the same tools in LangChain and CrewAI (29:45)**
The LangChain email agent chats with you and can read and send Gmail:
```
uv run 03-langchain/email_agent.py
```
I asked: What are the last three unread emails? Then the email and Slack agent, which gets the whole Slack server:
```
uv run 03-langchain/email_slack_agent.py
```
Can you summarize all emails from the last 24 hours and send a message in Slack to the #ai channel?
The CrewAI version (34:16) runs on its own and lists your email address and three latest subjects:
```
uv run 04-crewai/main.py
```

**7. Build the morning planner and schedule it (38:19)**
It reads today's ClickUp tasks and your Google Calendar and blocks out your day. First see your real tool names, then do a dry run that writes nothing, then let it write:
```
uv run 05-scheduled-agent/morning_planner.py --discover
uv run 05-scheduled-agent/morning_planner.py
uv run 05-scheduled-agent/morning_planner.py --apply
```
To schedule it, I didn't write the cron job myself. I asked Claude Code:
> Can you schedule the morning_planner.py with --apply on it every morning at 6 a.m. on my computer?
For 24/7 without your computer on (44:17), get a Hostinger KVM VPS, open its terminal, run Claude Code there and set up the same agent. The repo's deploy/README.md has the cron steps.

**8. Schedule a morning briefing with Claude Routines, no code (46:17)**
In the Claude app go to Code > Routines and describe it:
> I want to know all my tasks from ClickUp, what's on my calendar and a summary of my emails from the last 24 hours at 7 a.m. every morning.
Click Draft routine, then Create. In Arcade, make a gateway called Morning Assistant with Gmail, Google Calendar and ClickUp. Add it in Claude under Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector, connect and allow. Edit the routine (pencil icon), remove the other connectors, add Morning Assistant, save, then click Run now to test. Turn on push notifications to get the summary on your phone.

## Files and links
- Course code, all modules: https://github.com/tylerprogramming/arcade-course
- Copy-paste setup guide: https://github.com/tylerprogramming/arcade-course/blob/main/INSTALL.md
- VPS and cron guide: https://github.com/tylerprogramming/arcade-course/blob/main/deploy/README.md
- Arcade: https://www.arcade.dev/
- Arcade MCP gateways: https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/mcp-gateways
- Add Arcade to Claude Code, Desktop and Web: https://docs.arcade.dev/en/get-started/mcp-clients
- Claude custom connectors: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp

## If it breaks
- Gateway says "needs authentication": type /mcp, pick it, press Enter and allow it on Arcade.
- Claude uses the wrong ClickUp connection: name the gateway in your prompt ("for my ClickUp assistant").
- Custom server says no Arcade API key configured: run !arcade login inside Claude Code.
- Can't find your deployed server: it's under Servers in the dashboard, not MCP Gateways.
- Starring a repo failed because the Arcade GitHub connection wasn't allowed to star: add GitHub to the same gateway, save, then re-authenticate in /mcp.
- Old guides tell you to install langchain-arcade or crewai-arcade: don't. Install LangChain or CrewAI on their own plus the Arcade SDK. The repo already does this.
- The CrewAI agent errored on an empty page token with the OpenAI model: I pasted the error into Claude and it fixed it.
- The 6am job didn't run: your Mac was asleep. It runs when it wakes up, or keep it from sleeping, or use a VPS.
- Routine set to always allow: lock down tools that delete or trash things before you leave it running.

## In this lesson
You'll build one MCP gateway in arcade.dev that gives Claude Code access to Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Google Docs, Slack and ClickUp. Then you'll give it one prompt that reads an email thread, writes a Google Doc, files it in Drive and posts to Slack.

## Good to know
- Time: 15 to 20 minutes
- Cost: arcade.dev has a free plan to start, with paid plans above that.
- Level: Beginner. No code. You click tools in a web page and paste one command.
- Why not just use Claude's own connectors? For you on your own machine, those are fine. Arcade is for when you want other people using it, or an agent running 24/7. Google makes you re-authenticate every seven days unless you're a production-ready app. Arcade handles that for you.

## What you need
- Claude Code installed: https://claude.com/claude-code
- arcade.dev account (free to start): https://www.arcade.dev/
- The accounts you want to connect: Google (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs), Slack, ClickUp

**1. Sign in and create your first gateway (1:04)**
Sign in at arcade.dev, or create an account if it's your first time. On the left, click MCP Gateways. At the top right, click Create MCP Gateway. Give it a name. I called mine Google Calendar Assistant.

**2. Pick only the tools you need (1:41)**
Search for Gmail and click into its tools. These are the actual functions Claude will be able to call. I picked three: get emails, list emails, send emails. You can click All, but start small.

**3. Choose who can connect, then create it (2:18)**
Pick "Members of this project" if it's just you. The other option is external users who sign in with their own identity provider. Click Create MCP Gateway.

**4. Connect it to Claude Code and sign in (2:33)**
Arcade shows options for Cursor, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, or a plain MCP URL. Choose Claude Code and copy the command it gives you. Paste it into a fresh terminal. You should see "Added HTTP MCP server" with your gateway name. Don't share it. It's shown on screen in the video, and I deleted mine after recording.
Open Claude Code and type:

```
/mcp
```

Pick your gateway. It says it needs authentication. Press Enter, sign in with Google, click Allow. Then test it:

> List all my emails through the Google Calendar Assistant MCP server.

Naming the server makes sure it uses this one, not another Gmail connection you already have. Keep auto mode on.

**5. Build a bigger multi-tool gateway (4:06)**
Back in arcade.dev, go to MCP Gateways and create a new one. I called it Multi-Tool Assistant. I selected all tools for Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Drive (17 tools) and Slack. That came to 65 tools. Normally you'd narrow that down, but it shows it can do all of it at once. Pick Members of this project, create it, copy the Claude Code command, paste it in the terminal. Then in Claude Code, /mcp, pick Multi-Tool Assistant, authenticate.

**6. Turn off the servers you don't want it using (5:56)**
In /mcp, I disabled my other Gmail, Calendar, Drive and Slack connections. Now anything I ask about those apps goes through the Multi-Tool Assistant. Test it:

> Can you read the last 10 emails I had and then any specific calendar events I have for today?

**7. Run the five-step prompt (6:58)**
This is the one that touches four apps. Here's my prompt, cleaned up. Swap in your own email thread, folder and channel:

> Summarize my partnership emails with Blotato in Gmail, create a doc with that summary, save it to Google Drive in a folder named Blotato, and then send me a Slack message in the ai channel.

Google Drive tools can't write a document on their own. I added Google Docs to the gateway so it could create the doc, then move it into the folder. Check Drive and Slack to see the results.

**8. Add a new app to a live gateway (9:52)**
In arcade.dev, open your gateway and click the pencil to edit. Search for ClickUp, click All, then Save. Back in Claude Code, type /mcp, pick the gateway, and re-authenticate. Allow the new access. Then:

> How many tasks do I have?

**9. Add your team (10:47)**
In your Arcade project you can invite members. Each one signs in separately as their own user. Or set up your own sign-in provider with a client ID and secret. Either way you don't handle their tokens.

## Files and links
- arcade.dev: https://www.arcade.dev/
- arcade.dev pricing: https://www.arcade.dev/pricing
- Claude Code + Arcade docs: https://docs.arcade.dev/en/get-started/mcp-clients/claude-code
- Free content skills: https://free.tylerai.dev/content-automation

## If it breaks
- Gateway shows "needs authentication" in /mcp: press Enter on it and sign in again.
- You added a tool and Claude can't use it: any time you add tools to a gateway that already exists, re-authenticate in /mcp. I hit this with Google Docs.
- It uses the wrong Gmail or Slack connection: disable the other servers in /mcp, or name the gateway in your prompt.
- It can't create a doc in Drive: Drive tools alone can't write documents. Add Google Docs tools to the gateway, then re-authenticate.
- Too many tools to pick from: select only what the job needs. 65 tools works, but fewer is cleaner.
